class.name: SpawnSlot
class.brief_description: The resolved placement target for one player spawn.
class.description: A slot returns one question, "where does this player node go", and it returns it the same way whether the destination is a declared network scene or a plain branch of the tree. That is what lets a spawner be written once: it asks [method for_scene] for a slot and hands the player to [method place_player], instead of branching on whether the scene was declared. A slot resolves at the moment it is asked for, so it is a value to use now rather than a handle to keep. A session that declares no scene under the requested stem returns a slot that [method is_valid] rejects, and placing into it does nothing. [codeblock] var slot := SpawnSlot.for_scene(Netw.of(self), &"Arena") if slot.is_valid(): slot.place_player(player) [/codeblock]

method.name: for_scene
method.description: Resolves the slot for the scene [param session] declares under [param scene_stem]. This is the verb a spawner calls. A session declaring no such scene, and a null [param session], both return a slot [method is_valid] rejects rather than an error, so a spawner asks once and tests the result. [codeblock] var slot := SpawnSlot.for_scene(Netw.of(self), &"Arena") if slot.is_valid(): slot.place_player(player) [/codeblock]

method.name: get_scene
method.description: Returns the declared [NetwSceneHandle] this slot places into, or [code]null[/code] when it places under a plain parent instead.

method.name: has_scene
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when this slot carries a scene that is still declared. A handle to a scene the session has since dropped returns [code]false[/code], which is why this is asked rather than the handle being tested for null.

method.name: in_scene
method.description: Returns a slot that places players into [param scene] through [method NetwSceneHandle.add_player], so the spawned node is registered with the session rather than only parented.

method.name: is_valid
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when this slot still has somewhere to put a player: a declared scene, or a parent node that has not been freed.

method.name: place_player
method.description: Puts [param player] where this slot points. A scene slot adds it through [method NetwSceneHandle.add_player] as the [NetwEntity] the node carries; a parent slot adds it as a plain child. An invalid slot places nothing.

method.name: under
method.description: Returns a slot that adds players as children of [param parent], with no scene declaration involved. The parent is held weakly, so a slot outliving its parent reports [method is_valid] as [code]false[/code] instead of placing into a freed node.
